Question Text: A "Line Extension" involves which of the following actions within a Brand Strategy?
Option 1: Using an existing brand name to enter a completely new and unrelated product category.
Option 2: Using an existing brand name for new items in the same product category, like new flavors.
Option 3: Creating a new brand name for a product in a category the company is already in.
Option 4: Buying a competitor's brand and merging it into your own company's portfolio.

Question Text: What is "Brand Dilution" and why is it a concern in Brand Management?
Option 1: When a brand's logo is printed in a color that is too light to be seen by customers.
Option 2: When a brand name is used on too many products, weakening its core associations.
Option 3: When the company's stock price goes down because of a general market decline.
Option 4: When the product is diluted with water to save money on manufacturing costs.

Question Text: In the context of Rebranding, what is a "Refresh" compared to a "Full Rebrand"?
Option 1: A refresh changes the name, while a full rebrand only changes the color of the logo.
Option 2: A refresh involves minor visual updates, while a full rebrand involves a new name and mission.
Option 3: A refresh is only for digital brands, while a full rebrand is only for physical products.
Option 4: A refresh is done by the CEO, while a full rebrand is done by an outside agency.

Question Text: How does a "Brand Charter" assist in the process of Brand Equity Management?
Option 1: It is a legal document that lists all the shareholders and their ownership percentages.
Option 2: It serves as a guide for all marketing activities to ensure they align with brand values.
Option 3: It is a map showing all the locations where the brand's products are sold globally.
Option 4: It is a list of the names of every customer who has ever purchased the brand's product.

Question Text: Which of these best describes a Private Label Brand (also known as a Store Brand)?
Option 1: A brand that is owned by the manufacturer and sold in many different retail stores.
Option 2: A brand that is owned and sold exclusively by a specific retailer or wholesaler.
Option 3: A brand that is owned by a private individual and not by a registered corporation.
Option 4: A brand that is kept secret from the public and only sold to VIP customers.

Question Text: What is the primary benefit of "Ingredient Branding" (e.g., "Intel Inside" or "Gore-Tex")?
Option 1: It allows the ingredient supplier to hide their identity from the end consumer.
Option 2: It builds brand equity for a component that adds value to the host product.
Option 3: It makes the final product much cheaper to produce for the main manufacturer.
Option 4: It allows the main brand to stop advertising its own features to the customer.

Question Text: In Brand Positioning, what is a "Category Point of Parity"?
Option 1: A feature that makes the brand stand out as the absolute best in its category.
Option 2: A feature that is necessary for a brand to be considered a member of a specific category.
Option 3: A feature that is only found in brands that are failing in their specific category.
Option 4: A feature that the government requires for all products in a specific category.

Question Text: When a company undergoes Rebranding, why is it important to engage with "Brand Ambassadors" among the staff?
Option 1: To give them a reason to work longer hours without getting any additional pay.
Option 2: To turn influential employees into advocates who help drive the new brand culture.
Option 3: To make sure they don't tell the competition about the new logo before it launches.
Option 4: To ensure they all buy the new branded merchandise with their own money.

Question Text: Which of these is a qualitative research technique used in Brand Equity Management?
Option 1: A massive survey of 10,000 people using only multiple-choice questions.
Option 2: "Free Association" where consumers say what comes to mind when they hear the brand name.
Option 3: Analyzing the company's quarterly profit and loss statement from the last five years.
Option 4: Counting the number of people who walk past a billboard in a one-hour period.

Question Text: A "Brand Extension" is most likely to be successful when there is a high "Fit" between:
Option 1: The size of the parent brand's office and the size of the new product's packaging.
Option 2: The core brand's associations and the attributes of the new product category.
Option 3: The age of the brand's CEO and the age of the target audience for the new product.
Option 4: The number of words in the brand name and the number of features in the product.

Question Text: In Corporate Identity, what does "Corporate Behavior" refer to specifically?
Option 1: The way the logo is animated in television commercials and online videos.
Option 2: The actions of the company, including its social responsibility and treatment of staff.
Option 3: The way the company's delivery trucks are driven on public highways.
Option 4: The specific software programs used by the accounting department to track sales.

Question Text: What is the "Brand Promise" in the context of Brand Strategy?
Option 1: A legal guarantee that the product will never break during the user's lifetime.
Option 2: The fundamental benefit or experience that the brand guarantees to its customers.
Option 3: A promise made to investors that the brand will double its profit every single year.
Option 4: A contract signed by the customer promising they will never buy from a competitor.

Question Text: Which strategy involves using two or more brands to create a single product (e.g., a Hershey’s Brownie Mix by Betty Crocker)?
Option 1: Ingredient Branding
Option 2: Co-Branding
Option 3: Multi-Branding
Option 4: Brand Licensing

Question Text: Why would a firm use a "Multibrand Strategy" (having many brands in one category)?
Option 1: To reduce the total amount of money spent on marketing and advertising.
Option 2: To capture different segments and occupy more shelf space in retail stores.
Option 3: To make it easier for the CEO to remember the names of all the products.
Option 4: To satisfy a government regulation that requires every company to have ten brands.

Question Text: What is "Brand Salience" and why is it important in the Brand Positioning process?
Option 1: It is the price of the brand compared to the average price in the market.
Option 2: It is how often and how easily a brand is thought of under various purchase situations.
Option 3: It is the legal protection the brand has against other companies using its logo.
Option 4: It is the total number of employees the brand has in its marketing department.

Question Text: In Brand Equity Management, "Brand Imagery" refers to:
Option 1: The technical specifications and functional performance of the product.
Option 2: The extrinsic properties of the product, including the way the brand attempts to meet psychological needs.
Option 3: The actual photographs used in the brand's latest social media advertising campaign.
Option 4: The list of all the materials used to build the brand's physical retail locations.

Question Text: When a company uses "Brand Licensing," what is it essentially doing?
Option 1: Selling the entire company to another firm but keeping the name on the door.
Option 2: Letting another firm use its brand name on products for a fee or royalty.
Option 3: Giving away its products for free to anyone who wants to use the brand name.
Option 4: Hiring a new advertising agency to create a new logo for the brand.

Question Text: What is the main goal of a Corporate Identity manual (or Brand Guidelines)?
Option 1: To provide a history of the company's founders and their early business successes.
Option 2: To ensure all visual and verbal communications are consistent across all touchpoints.
Option 3: To list the phone numbers of all the suppliers the company uses for manufacturing.
Option 4: To show the employees where they are allowed to park their cars at the office.

Question Text: In a Rebranding Strategy, "Brand Migration" is the process of:
Option 1: Moving the company's headquarters from one country to another to save on taxes.
Option 2: Systematically transitioning customers from an old brand name to a new one.
Option 3: Hiring all the employees from a competitor's brand to work for your own brand.
Option 4: Changing the website address of the brand without telling any of the customers.

Question Text: Which of the following is an "Internal Point of Parity" in Brand Positioning?
Option 1: A feature that the company's employees believe is the best in the entire world.
Option 2: A standard that a brand must meet to be seen as a legitimate player by its own staff.
Option 3: A feature that is identical to what the competitors are offering in the market.
Option 4: A legal requirement for the product to be sold in certain international countries.

Question Text: What is "Brand Personality"?
Option 1: The personality of the CEO who founded the brand many years ago.
Option 2: The set of human characteristics associated with a brand name.
Option 3: The way the brand's employees talk to each other in the breakroom.
Option 4: The physical appearance of the brand's mascot in television commercials.

Question Text: In Brand Equity Management, what is "Brand Knowledge"?
Option 1: Everything the marketing manager knows about the brand's financial history.
Option 2: The thoughts, feelings, images, and experiences consumers associate with the brand.
Option 3: The technical data sheets that explain how the brand's products are manufactured.
Option 4: The list of all the competitors that the brand is currently fighting in the market.

Question Text: A "Brand Audit" is usually composed of two steps: the Brand Inventory and the ________.
Option 1: Brand Financials
Option 2: Brand Exploratory
Option 3: Brand Advertising
Option 4: Brand Licensing

Question Text: Why is "Differentiation" the core of any successful Brand Strategy?
Option 1: Because it allows the brand to look exactly like the market leader in the category.
Option 2: Because it gives consumers a specific reason to choose one brand over another.
Option 3: Because it is a legal requirement for getting a trademark for a new brand name.
Option 4: Because it helps the company save money on its manufacturing and labor costs.

Question Text: What does the "Brand Value Chain" model help marketers understand?
Option 1: The physical process of shipping products from the factory to the retail store.
Option 2: How marketing activities create value that eventually leads to financial performance.
Option 3: The hierarchy of employees in the marketing department from junior to senior.
Option 4: The list of all the raw materials used to create the brand's primary product.

Question Text: In Rebranding, what is "Visual Identity"?
Option 1: The company's mission statement and its core values and ethical beliefs.
Option 2: The logo, typography, and color palette that represent the brand visually.
Option 3: The way the company's office building is designed and decorated on the inside.
Option 4: The physical appearance of the people who buy the brand's products.

Question Text: What is "Brand Awareness"?
Option 1: Knowing the name of the CEO of the company that makes the brand.
Option 2: The extent to which consumers are familiar with the qualities or image of a brand.
Option 3: The number of advertisements the brand runs on television every single month.
Option 4: The physical size of the brand's logo on the front of the product's packaging.

Question Text: Which of these is a risk of Brand Extension?

Option 2: The new product might be so good that people stop buying the old product.

Question Text: In Brand Positioning, a "Point of Difference" must be:
Option 1: Something that the competitors are also doing, but just a little bit better.
Option 2: Something that is desirable to the customer and deliverable by the company.
Option 3: Something that is so unique that no customer actually wants or needs it.
Option 4: Something that the company can only do for a very short period of time.

Question Text: What is "Brand Loyalty"?
Option 1: When a customer buys a brand because it is the only one available in the store.
Option 2: The tendency of some consumers to continue buying the same brand of goods.
Option 3: When a company gives away free products to people to make them like the brand.
Option 4: The legal contract a customer signs to only buy products from one specific company.

Question Text: A "Sub-brand" is a Brand Strategy where:
Option 1: A new brand is created that has no connection to the parent brand at all.
Option 2: A new brand is combined with an existing parent brand (e.g., Apple iPhone).
Option 3: A brand is sold to a smaller company that operates in a different country.
Option 4: A brand name is used for a product that is inferior to the main product.

Question Text: In Brand Equity Management, "Brand Recall" is:
Option 1: The ability of consumers to confirm prior exposure to the brand when given a cue.
Option 2: The ability of consumers to retrieve the brand from memory when given the category.
Option 3: The process of taking a product off the shelves because it is dangerous to use.
Option 4: The number of times a customer calls the company to complain about a product.

Question Text: What is the purpose of "Brand Positioning"?
Option 1: To make sure the brand is placed on the top shelf in every single retail store.
Option 2: To occupy a distinct and valued place in the target customer's mind.
Option 3: To ensure the brand's logo is always positioned on the left side of an advertisement.
Option 4: To find the best geographical location to build the brand's main factory.

Question Text: Which of these is a benefit of having strong Brand Equity?
Option 1: The company can charge more for its products than its competitors.
Option 2: The company can spend less money on advertising because people already know it.
Option 3: The company can more easily launch new products under the same brand name.
Option 4: All of the above are benefits of having strong brand equity.

Question Text: In Corporate Identity, "Corporate Image" is:
Option 1: How the company wants to be seen by the public and its customers.
Option 2: How the company is actually perceived by the public and its customers.
Option 3: The photographs of the company's board of directors in the annual report.
Option 4: The logo and the visual design of the company's primary website.

Question Text: What is "Brand Essence"?
Option 1: The physical smell of the brand's product when it is first taken out of the box.
Option 2: The single most important heart and soul of the brand's identity.
Option 3: The list of all the ingredients used to make the brand's primary product.
Option 4: The total amount of money the brand has in its bank account at any time.

Question Text: Why would a company use Rebranding to target a new demographic?
Option 1: Because the old demographic has stopped buying products altogether.
Option 2: Because the current brand image is not appealing or relevant to the new group.
Option 3: Because the government has passed a law saying they must target a new group.
Option 4: Because the marketing manager wants to try something new and exciting.

Question Text: In Brand Strategy, what is "Brand Architecture"?
Option 1: The physical design of the company's headquarters and its retail stores.
Option 2: The way a company organizes and structures its various brands and products.
Option 3: The process of building a brand from the ground up using a construction metaphor.
Option 4: The list of all the architects who have worked on the company's buildings.

Question Text: What is "Brand Associations"?
Option 1: The group of companies that work together to promote a specific industry.
Option 2: Anything deep-seated in a customer's mind about a particular brand.
Option 3: The list of all the celebrities who have ever used the brand's products.
Option 4: The social clubs that employees of the brand are allowed to join.

Question Text: In Brand Equity Management, "Brand Recognition" is:
Option 1: The ability of consumers to confirm prior exposure to the brand when given a cue.
Option 2: The ability of consumers to remember the brand name without any help.
Option 3: An award given to the brand for having the best advertisement of the year.
Option 4: The process of the government recognizing the brand as a legal entity.

Question Text: What is "Brand Portfolio"?
Option 1: A physical folder that contains all the brand's marketing materials.
Option 2: The set of all brands and brand lines a particular firm offers for sale.
Option 3: The total value of all the stocks and bonds owned by the company.
Option 4: A collection of photographs of the brand's products in use by customers.

Question Text: Why is "Emotional Connection" important in Brand Strategy?
Option 1: Because it makes customers ignore the price of the product entirely.
Option 2: Because it creates a deeper bond and higher loyalty than functional benefits alone.
Option 3: Because it is easier to create an emotion than it is to create a good product.
Option 4: Because emotions are the only thing that people care about when they are shopping.

Question Text: In Rebranding, what is a "Logo Redesign"?
Option 1: Changing the company's entire mission, vision, and core values.
Option 2: Updating or completely changing the visual symbol of the brand.
Option 3: Changing the name of the company to something completely different.
Option 4: Moving the logo from the top of the page to the bottom of the page.

Question Text: What is "Brand Communication"?
Option 1: The way the employees of the brand talk to each other in the office.
Option 2: The various ways a brand sends messages about itself to its audience.
Option 3: The phone system used by the brand's customer service department.
Option 4: The legal documents the brand sends to the government every year.

Question Text: In Brand Positioning, a "Brand Map" helps to:
Option 1: Find the physical locations of all the brand's competitors in a city.
Option 2: Visualize how a brand is perceived relative to its competitors.
Option 3: Map out the journey of a customer from the factory to the store.
Option 4: Show the geographical areas where the brand is most popular.

Question Text: What is "Brand Consistency"?
Option 1: Using the same logo for at least one hundred years without any changes.
Option 2: Ensuring the brand's message and look are the same across all channels.
Option 3: Making sure the brand's products are always the exact same weight.
Option 4: Only selling the brand's products in one specific type of retail store.

Question Text: In Brand Equity Management, "Brand Feelings" are:
Option 1: The physical sensations a customer has when they touch the product.
Option 2: Customers' emotional responses and reactions with respect to the brand.
Option 3: The feelings the brand's employees have about their current salaries.
Option 4: The emotions the CEO feels when the brand's stock price goes up.

Question Text: What is "Brand Extension Profitability"?
Option 1: The total amount of money the company makes from its original product.
Option 2: The potential for a new product under an existing brand to be financially successful.
Option 3: The amount of money the company saves by not creating a new brand.
Option 4: The percentage of the marketing budget spent on a new brand extension.

Question Text: In Corporate Identity, "Corporate Culture" is:
Option 1: The types of art and music that are popular in the country where the company is.
Option 2: The shared values, beliefs, and behaviors of the people within the company.
Option 3: The museum that the company sponsors in its local community.
Option 4: The specific way the company's employees dress for formal events.

Question Text: What is "Brand Narratives"?
Option 1: The stories that a brand tells to connect with its audience and build its identity.
Option 2: The technical reports that the brand's engineers write about the products.
Option 3: The legal documents that explain the history of the brand's trademarks.
Option 4: The list of all the books that have been written about the brand's history.

Question Text: Why would a brand use "Nostalgia" in its Brand Strategy?
Option 1: Because the brand has no new products and needs to sell old ones.
Option 2: To create a sense of comfort and trust by tapping into positive past memories.
Option 3: Because old advertisements are much cheaper to run than new advertisements.
Option 4: To show the customers how much better the brand was in the past.

Question Text: In Rebranding, what is "Brand Repositioning"?
Option 1: Moving the brand's products to a different aisle in the retail store.
Option 2: Changing the target market or core benefit of a brand to change its image.
Option 3: Changing the physical location of the brand's headquarters to a new city.
Option 4: Changing the brand's logo but keeping everything else exactly the same.

Question Text: What is "Brand Value"?
Option 1: The physical cost of all the materials used to make the brand's products.
Option 2: The financial worth of the brand as an intangible asset on the balance sheet.
Option 3: The amount of money a customer thinks the brand's product is worth.
Option 4: The total number of products the brand has sold since it was founded.

Question Text: In Brand Positioning, "Frame of Reference" is:
Option 1: The physical frame that is put around the brand's logo in advertisements.
Option 2: The category or set of competitors that the brand is being compared to.
Option 3: The specific time frame during which the brand's positioning will be used.
Option 4: The list of all the people who have influenced the brand's positioning.

Question Text: What is "Brand Heritage"?
Option 1: The history and tradition of a brand that adds to its credibility and value.
Option 2: The list of all the buildings that the brand has owned over the years.
Option 3: The nationality of the person who originally founded the brand.
Option 4: The amount of money the brand's founder left to their children.

Question Text: In Brand Equity Management, "Brand Performance" is:
Option 1: How well the brand's advertisements perform in terms of views and likes.
Option 2: How well the product or service meets customers' functional needs.
Option 3: The speed at which the brand's products are delivered to the customers.
Option 4: The percentage of the brand's employees who are happy with their jobs.

Question Text: What is "Brand Personality Dimension: Sincerity"?
Option 1: A brand that is seen as being very honest, wholesome, and cheerful.
Option 2: A brand that is seen as being very exciting, daring, and spirited.
Option 3: A brand that is seen as being very reliable, intelligent, and successful.
Option 4: A brand that is seen as being very upper-class, glamorous, and charming.

Question Text: In Corporate Identity, "Corporate Communication" is:
Option 1: The way the employees talk to each other using the internal email system.
Option 2: The ways a company communicates with its internal and external stakeholders.
Option 3: The phone calls the company makes to its customers to sell them new products.
Option 4: The advertisements the company runs on television and in magazines.

Question Text: Why is "Brand Protection" important in Brand Management?
Option 1: To make sure the brand's products are protected from damage during shipping.
Option 2: To prevent other companies from using the brand's identity and stealing its value.
Option 3: To protect the brand's employees from being hired by other companies.
Option 4: To protect the brand's CEO from being interviewed by the media.

Question Text: What is "Brand Community"?
Option 1: The neighborhood where the brand's main office is located.
Option 2: A group of consumers who share a common interest in and loyalty to a brand.
Option 3: The group of companies that supply materials to the brand's factory.
Option 4: The social media platform where the brand has the most followers.

Question Text: In Brand Strategy, what is "Brand Stretching"?
Option 1: Using the brand name on a product that is in a much higher or lower price range.
Option 2: Printing the brand's logo on a piece of material that can be stretched out.
Option 3: Making the brand's advertisements longer so that they reach more people.
Option 4: Increasing the size of the brand's logo on all of its marketing materials.

Question Text: What is "Brand Touchpoints"?
Option 1: The physical locations where a customer can touch the brand's products.
Option 2: Any point of interaction between a brand and a customer.
Option 3: The number of times a customer calls the brand's customer service line.
Option 4: The physical contact information for the brand's marketing department.

Question Text: In Rebranding, what is "Brand Equity Transfer"?
Option 1: The process of selling the brand's equity to another company for a profit.
Option 2: Moving the positive associations from an old brand to a new or updated brand.
Option 3: Calculating the exact value of the brand's equity before it is rebranded.
Option 4: Changing the brand's equity into a different currency for international sales.

Question Text: What is "Brand Evangelism"?
Option 1: A type of religious marketing that uses brand names to promote beliefs.
Option 2: When customers are so loyal to a brand that they actively promote it to others.
Option 3: When a brand's employees are required to talk about the brand at church.
Option 4: A marketing strategy that only targets people who are very religious.

Question Text: In Brand Positioning, a "Tagline" is:
Option 1: A short, catchy phrase that conveys the brand's core message or positioning.
Option 2: The legal name of the company that is printed at the bottom of an ad.
Option 3: A list of all the product's features that is printed on the packaging.
Option 4: The price of the product that is written on a tag in the retail store.

Question Text: What is "Brand Cohesion"?
Option 1: When all the parts of a brand work together to create a unified and strong image.
Option 2: When a brand's products are made of the same materials so they stick together.
Option 3: When a brand's employees all work in the same office building together.
Option 4: When a brand's marketing budget is spent on only one type of advertisement.

Question Text: In Brand Equity Management, "Brand Meaning" is:
Option 1: The definition of the brand's name as it is found in the dictionary.
Option 2: The set of associations and perceptions that consumers have about a brand.
Option 3: The total amount of money that the brand's name is worth to the company.
Option 4: The message that the brand's CEO wants to send to the company's investors.

Question Text: What is "Brand Differentiation"?
Option 1: Making the brand's logo a different color than the logos of its competitors.
Option 2: Making the brand's products stand out from the competition in a meaningful way.
Option 3: Selling the brand's products in different countries around the entire world.
Option 4: Having different prices for the brand's products in different retail stores.

Question Text: In Corporate Identity, "Visual Verbal Synergy" is:
Option 1: When the brand's logo and its advertisements are both very loud and colorful.
Option 2: When the visual and written parts of a brand's communication work together.
Option 3: When the brand's employees all speak the same language in the office.
Option 4: When the brand's website and its social media pages use the same fonts.

Question Text: Why is "Long-term Thinking" critical in Branding & Brand Management?
Option 1: Because it takes a very long time to design a new logo for a large company.
Option 2: Because building and maintaining a strong brand is a process that takes years.
Option 3: Because the government requires all brand strategies to be at least ten years long.
Option 4: Because the CEO of the company wants to stay in their job for a very long time.

Question Text: During the 'Introduction' phase of the Product Life Cycle, which of the following is the primary marketing objective for a brand manager?

Option 3: To reduce expenditures and milk the brand for as much profit as possible before exit.

Question Text: In the context of New Product Development (NPD), what is the primary purpose of the 'Concept Testing' stage before technical development?

Option 2: To test the physical durability of the prototype under extreme environmental conditions.
Option 3: To evaluate consumer reaction to a proposed product idea before investing in full-scale R&D.
Option 4: To design the promotional campaign and select the appropriate media channels for launch.

Question Text: When a company uses a 'Penetration Pricing' strategy for a new product launch, what is the most likely intended outcome?
Option 1: To signal premium quality and exclusivity to high-end consumers in a niche market.
Option 2: To recover high Research and Development costs as quickly as possible through high margins.
Option 3: To gain significant market share rapidly by setting a low initial price to attract many buyers.
Option 4: To match the pricing of the market leader exactly to avoid a price war in the industry.

Question Text: Which of the following best describes the 'Growth' stage of the Product Life Cycle in terms of competition and profit?
Option 1: Sales are flat, profits are at their peak, and competition is starting to exit the market.
Option 2: Sales rise rapidly, profits begin to peak, and new competitors enter with improved features.
Option 3: Sales decline, profits turn into losses, and only the most loyal customers remain.
Option 4: Sales are non-existent, and the company is incurring heavy losses due to initial setup costs.

Question Text: A 'Skimming Pricing' strategy is most effective under which of the following market conditions during a launch?
Option 1: When the product is a commodity with many substitutes and the market is highly price-sensitive.
Option 2: When the product’s quality and image support a high price and there are enough buyers.
Option 3: When there is no intellectual property protection and competitors can enter the market easily.
Option 4: When the primary goal is to achieve mass-market adoption within the first month of launch.

Question Text: In portfolio management, what does the 'Boston Consulting Group (BCG) Matrix' use as its two primary dimensions for analysis?
Option 1: Internal Strengths and External Opportunities of the specific product line.
Option 2: Relative Market Share and the Growth Rate of the specific market industry.

Question Text: During the 'Maturity' stage of the product lifecycle, which strategy is most commonly used to maintain sales volume?

Question Text: What is the main difference between 'Value-Based Pricing' and 'Cost-Plus Pricing' in a product management context?
Option 1: Value-based uses consumer perception of value, while cost-plus uses the cost of production.
Option 2: Value-based is only for luxury goods, while cost-plus is only for government contracts.
Option 3: Value-based pricing is always lower than cost-plus pricing to ensure higher sales volume.
Option 4: Cost-plus pricing ignores competition, while value-based pricing ignores the consumer.

Question Text: In the 'Stage-Gate' model of product development, what is the primary role of a 'Gate' between two development stages?
Option 1: To provide a location for team members to socialize and discuss non-work related topics.
Option 2: To serve as a checkpoint where the project is reviewed to decide if it should continue.
Option 3: To act as a physical barrier in the factory to prevent unauthorized access to prototypes.
Option 4: To ensure that the marketing department does not interfere with the engineering process.

Question Text: Which of the following best describes 'Product Cannibalization' within a company's existing portfolio?
Option 1: When a competitor releases a similar product that steals your existing market share.
Option 2: When a new product launch reduces the sales volume or market share of an existing product.
Option 3: When a company decides to stop selling a product because it is no longer profitable.
Option 4: When a product’s raw materials are repurposed for the manufacturing of a different item.

Question Text: What is 'Psychological Pricing' and how is it typically applied in a retail product environment?
Option 1: Setting prices based on the emotional state of the salesperson at the time of the transaction.
Option 2: Setting prices that have a specific psychological impact, such as $9.99 instead of $10.00.
Option 3: Pricing products based on the IQ level of the target demographic identified in the research.
Option 4: Charging different prices to different people based on their perceived ability to pay.

Question Text: In a 'Product Bundle' pricing strategy, what is the primary motivation for the seller to offer multiple items together?
Option 1: To increase the perceived cost of the individual items so they can be sold for more later.
Option 2: To encourage customers to buy more than they intended by offering a lower combined price.
Option 3: To hide the fact that one of the products in the bundle is actually defective or expired.
Option 4: To comply with government regulations regarding the maximum price of single items.

Question Text: When performing a SWOT analysis for a new product, which of the following would be considered a 'Threat'?
Option 1: A unique patented technology that gives the product a competitive advantage in the market.
Option 2: An emerging competitor who has developed a similar technology at a lower production cost.
Option 3: A highly skilled internal marketing team with experience in launching successful products.
Option 4: A growing trend among consumers who are looking for exactly the type of product you have.

Question Text: What is the primary focus of 'Lean Product Development' compared to traditional waterfall development methods?
Option 1: Focusing on long-term planning and extensive documentation before any testing begins.
Option 2: Minimizing waste and maximizing value through iterative testing and rapid prototyping.
Option 3: Hiring as many people as possible to ensure that the project is finished ahead of schedule.
Option 4: Spending the majority of the budget on high-end celebrity endorsements for the launch.

Question Text: If a product is categorized as a 'Question Mark' in the BCG Matrix, what is the recommended strategic action?
Option 1: Harvest the product immediately to fund other 'Stars' in the company's portfolio.
Option 2: Divest or invest heavily to turn it into a 'Star' before the market growth slows down.
Option 3: Maintain the status quo and do not invest any further capital into its development.
Option 4: Lower the price significantly to turn it into a 'Cash Cow' as quickly as possible.

Question Text: Which of the following is a characteristic of 'Product Line Filling' as a portfolio management tactic?
Option 1: Adding new products to the line that are priced significantly higher than existing ones.
Option 2: Adding more items within the current range of the line to keep competitors out of gaps.
Option 3: Deleting products that have become obsolete due to the introduction of newer technology.
Option 4: Rebranding the entire line with a new logo to appeal to a younger demographic group.

Question Text: What is the concept of 'Price Elasticity of Demand' and why is it important for a Product Manager?
Option 1: It measures how much the quantity demanded of a product changes when its price changes.
Option 2: It measures the physical flexibility of the product packaging under high pressure or heat.
Option 3: It measures the speed at which competitors react to a change in the product's retail price.
Option 4: It measures the emotional attachment a customer has to a brand regardless of the price.

Question Text: In the 'Diffusion of Innovation' theory, which group of consumers is the last to adopt a new product?
Option 1: The Innovators, who are eager to try new ideas and take risks with new technology.
Option 2: The Laggards, who are tradition-bound and suspicious of any new product changes.
Option 3: The Early Majority, who adopt new ideas just before the average person in the market.
Option 4: The Late Majority, who are skeptical and only adopt after the majority have tried it.

Question Text: What does 'Product Breadth' refer to in the context of a company's total product mix?
Option 1: The total number of individual items offered within a specific product line or category.
Option 2: The number of different product lines that a company carries in its overall portfolio.
Option 3: The physical dimensions of the product's packaging and how much shelf space it takes.
Option 4: The number of different versions of each product, such as various sizes or colors.

Question Text: A 'Loss Leader' pricing strategy involves selling a product at a price below its cost. What is the goal?
Option 1: To quickly go out of business so the company can claim a tax write-off for the losses.
Option 2: To attract customers into a store in the hope they will buy other, more profitable items.
Option 3: To trick the competition into lowering their prices so they also lose money on sales.
Option 4: To demonstrate the high quality of the product by showing it is worth more than its price.

Question Text: What is a 'Minimum Viable Product' (MVP) in the context of new product development and launches?
Option 1: The version of a new product that allows a team to collect the most validated learning.
Option 2: The cheapest possible version of a product that can be manufactured using scrap parts.
Option 3: A product that has every possible feature included to ensure it beats all the competitors.
Option 4: A product that has been fully tested and is ready for international mass-market distribution.

Question Text: In 'Dynamic Pricing,' how are the prices of products or services typically determined?
Option 1: By a fixed government regulation that prevents prices from changing more than once a year.
Option 2: By algorithms that adjust prices in real-time based on demand, supply, and competitor data.
Option 3: By the intuition of the store manager based on how many people are walking in the door.
Option 4: By a democratic vote of the customers who are currently looking at the product online.

Question Text: Which of the following is an example of 'Co-Branding' as a product management strategy?
Option 1: A company launching two different products under the same brand name in one month.
Option 2: Two established brands working together on a single product to leverage both brand names.
Option 3: A company changing its name to sound more like its most successful product's name.
Option 4: A brand hiring a celebrity to appear in a television commercial for a new product.

Question Text: What is 'Product Positioning' and how does it relate to the target market's perception?
Option 1: The physical location of the product on the retail shelf relative to the competitors.
Option 2: The act of designing a company's offering to occupy a distinct place in the target's mind.
Option 3: The process of deciding which geographic regions the product will be shipped to first.
Option 4: The way a product is photographed for the catalog to make it look as large as possible.

Question Text: When a company uses 'Geographic Pricing,' what factors are they primarily considering?
Option 1: The age and income level of the people living in a specific neighborhood or city.
Option 2: Differences in costs of delivery and local market conditions in different locations.
Option 3: The physical weight of the product and how it affects the fuel efficiency of trucks.
Option 4: The language spoken in a specific region and how it affects the product's name.

Question Text: In the context of 'Product Cannibalization,' when might a company intentionally cannibalize its own products?
Option 1: Never, because it always leads to a decrease in total company profits and market value.
Option 2: When they want to prevent a competitor from entering the market with a similar product.
Option 3: When they have too much inventory of the old product and want to force people to buy it.
Option 4: When the marketing team makes a mistake in the launch timing and releases both at once.

Question Text: What is the 'Total Product Concept' and what does it suggest about what customers are buying?
Option 1: That customers only care about the physical features and the raw materials of the item.
Option 2: That a product is a bundle of physical, service, and symbolic attributes that satisfy needs.
Option 3: That the only thing that matters in a product's success is the price at which it is sold.
Option 4: That a company should produce as many different products as possible to satisfy everyone.

Question Text: How does 'Brand Equity' affect the pricing strategy of a product manager for a new launch?
Option 1: High brand equity allows a company to charge a premium price compared to competitors.
Option 2: High brand equity requires a company to keep prices low to reward loyal customers.
Option 3: Brand equity has no impact on pricing because consumers only care about the features.
Option 4: High brand equity means the product manager does not need to set a price at all.

Question Text: Which of the following is a primary risk of 'Over-segmenting' a market for a new product launch?
Option 1: The segments may become too small to be profitable or to justify a unique marketing mix.
Option 2: The company will have too many customers and will not be able to fulfill all the orders.
Option 3: The product will become so popular that the government will declare it a monopoly.
Option 4: The competitors will be confused and will not know which product to copy first.

Question Text: A company decides to 'Harvest' a product line. What does this strategic decision typically involve?
Option 1: Investing heavily in new features to try and restart the growth phase of the product.
Option 2: Reducing all costs associated with the product to maximize short-term cash flow.
Option 3: Increasing the price of the product to its highest ever level to attract luxury buyers.
Option 4: Hiring a new team to completely redesign the product from the ground up for kids.

Question Text: In the 'New Product Development' process, what happens during the 'Business Analysis' stage?
Option 1: Engineers build the first working prototype to see if the product is actually possible.
Option 2: The company reviews sales, costs, and profit projections to see if they meet objectives.
Option 3: The marketing team creates the first advertisement and shows it to a focus group.
Option 4: The product is launched in a small geographic area to see how many people buy it.

Question Text: What is 'Product Depth' in the context of a company's product portfolio management?
Option 1: The total number of different product categories the company competes in globally.
Option 2: The number of versions offered of each product in the line, such as sizes or flavors.
Option 3: The physical depth of the product packaging when it is placed on a standard shelf.
Option 4: The level of technical complexity involved in the manufacturing of the product line.

Question Text: How does 'Competitor-Based Pricing' differ from other pricing strategies in a crowded market?
Option 1: It focuses on the internal costs of the company rather than what others are doing.
Option 2: It sets prices based primarily on the prices charged by the company's competitors.
Option 3: It ignores the competitors and sets prices based on the lunar calendar cycles.
Option 4: It lets the customers decide the price through an online auction for every item.

Question Text: In the 'Maturity' stage, why might a company choose to use 'Market Modification'?
Option 1: To find new users or new market segments for the existing product to boost sales.
Option 2: To change the physical ingredients of the product to make it cheaper to produce.
Option 3: To close down all the factories and move production to a different country entirely.
Option 4: To change the name of the company to distance itself from a failing product line.

Question Text: What is the primary advantage of 'Test Marketing' a new product in a specific city before a national launch?
Option 1: It allows the company to reach the maximum number of customers as quickly as possible.
Option 2: It provides a real-world test of the marketing plan and the product's potential success.
Option 3: It ensures that the competition will not find out about the product until it is too late.
Option 4: It is the cheapest way to launch a product because advertising is free in small cities.

Question Text: Which of the following is an example of 'Captive-Product Pricing' in a business model?
Option 1: Selling a car at a very low price and then charging high prices for the engine oil.
Option 2: Selling a printer at a low price but charging high prices for the replacement ink cartridges.
Option 3: Selling a bundle of three products for the price of two to clear out old stock.
Option 4: Selling luxury watches in a locked case to make them seem more valuable to buyers.

Question Text: What is the role of a 'Product Champion' within a large corporation's development team?
Option 1: To be the person who physically builds the product on the assembly line every day.
Option 2: To be the person who advocates for the product and helps overcome internal resistance.
Option 3: To be the celebrity who is paid to talk about the product on social media platforms.
Option 4: To be the customer who has bought the most units of the product in the last year.

Question Text: In portfolio management, what is a 'Cash Cow' and how should its profits be used?
Option 1: A product with high market share in a slow-growth market; profits should fund other units.
Option 2: A product with low market share in a fast-growth market; profits should be reinvested.
Option 3: A product that is losing money and should be sold to another company as soon as possible.
Option 4: A product that has just been launched and is expected to become very popular soon.

Question Text: What is 'Conjoint Analysis' used for in the product development and pricing process?
Option 1: To determine how consumers value different attributes or features of a potential product.
Option 2: To analyze the chemical composition of a competitor's product to see how it works.
Option 3: To predict the exact day that a product will reach the end of its life cycle stage.
Option 4: To coordinate the shipping schedules of multiple products to different warehouses.

Question Text: Why would a company use 'Image Pricing' for two versions of essentially the same product?
Option 1: To make one product look bad so that customers will feel sorry for it and buy it.
Option 2: To signal different quality levels or prestige to different customer segments.
Option 3: To confuse the customers so they don't know which product is actually the better one.
Option 4: To satisfy a legal requirement that no two products can ever have the same price.

Question Text: In 'Product Life Cycle' management, what is 'Decline' and what usually causes it?
Option 1: When sales drop significantly due to technological advances or shifts in consumer tastes.
Option 2: When the company decides to double the price of the product to see if people still buy it.
Option 3: When the product becomes so popular that the company cannot keep up with the demand.
Option 4: When the government mandates that the product can no longer be sold in certain states.

Question Text: What is the 'Kano Model' used for in product feature prioritization and development?
Option 1: To calculate the exact cost of adding a new button to an electronic device's design.
Option 2: To categorize product features based on how they affect customer satisfaction.
Option 3: To determine the best color for a product's logo based on the psychological impact.
Option 4: To track the physical location of every product in the supply chain at all times.

Question Text: Which of the following is a drawback of using a 'Product-Centric' rather than a 'Customer-Centric' approach?
Option 1: The company might create a technically perfect product that nobody actually wants to buy.
Option 2: The company will spend too much time talking to customers and not enough time building.
Option 3: The product will be too cheap because the company is focusing on the product's quality.
Option 4: The marketing team will have nothing to do because the product will sell itself.

Question Text: What is 'Price Discrimination' and is it always illegal in the context of marketing?
Option 1: Charging different prices to different customers for the same product; it's often legal.
Option 2: Charging a higher price to people who look like they have more money; it's always illegal.
Option 3: Giving a discount to people who are your friends; it's a violation of company policy.
Option 4: Setting the price of a product based on the weight of the customer; it's always legal.

Question Text: In the context of the 'Product-Market Expansion Grid,' what is 'Market Penetration'?
Option 1: Selling new products to the existing market segments that the company already serves.
Option 2: Selling existing products to new market segments, such as different countries or ages.
Option 3: Increasing sales of current products to current market segments without changing the product.
Option 4: Developing entirely new products for entirely new markets where the company has no experience.

Question Text: How does 'Crowdsourcing' help in the new product development and launch process?
Option 1: By letting the public vote on which company should be allowed to produce the product.
Option 2: By obtaining ideas, feedback, or funding from a large group of people, usually online.
Option 3: By forcing the employees to work for free on their weekends to finish the product.
Option 4: By hiring a crowd of actors to stand in line at the store on the day the product launches.

Question Text: What is 'Product Differentiation' and why is it crucial for a brand's long-term success?
Option 1: Making a product appear similar to the market leader so customers will buy it by mistake.
Option 2: Highlighting unique features or benefits that make a product stand out from competitors.
Option 3: Pricing a product exactly the same as everyone else to avoid any brand confusion.
Option 4: Making sure that every single unit of the product looks exactly like every other unit.

Question Text: During a 'Soft Launch,' what is the primary goal of the product management team?
Option 1: To generate the maximum amount of buzz and media attention possible in one day.
Option 2: To release the product to a limited audience to find bugs and gather initial feedback.
Option 3: To sell as many units as possible before the competitors realize what is happening.
Option 4: To clear out the old inventory of the previous version of the product at a discount.

Question Text: What is 'Reference Pricing' and how do consumers use it when evaluating a product's cost?
Option 1: The price that a consumer has in mind and refers to when looking at a particular product.
Option 2: The price that is written in the official reference manual for the specific industry.
Option 3: The price that the salesperson mentions first to anchor the customer's expectations.
Option 4: The average price of all the products that are currently being sold in the same store.

Question Text: In the 'Diffusion of Innovation,' what characterizes the 'Early Adopters' group?
Option 1: They are the very first to try an idea; they are often risk-takers and tech-savvy.
Option 2: They are opinion leaders who adopt new ideas early but carefully; they guide others.
Option 3: They are the skeptical majority who only adopt after the product is a proven success.
Option 4: They are the last to adopt and usually do so only because the old product is gone.

Question Text: Which of the following is a key element of 'Sustainable Product Development'?
Option 1: Using the cheapest possible materials regardless of their impact on the environment.
Option 2: Designing products that have a minimal negative impact on the environment and society.
Option 3: Making products that last forever so that the customer never has to buy a new one.
Option 4: Packaging products in large plastic boxes to protect them during the shipping process.

Question Text: What is 'Product Mix Consistency' and why does it matter for a brand's image?
Option 1: How closely related the various product lines are in end-use, production, or channels.
Option 2: Whether all the products in the mix are sold for exactly the same retail price.
Option 3: Whether the company uses the same color of paint on all its office buildings and cars.
Option 4: How many different languages the product manuals are translated into for the launch.

Question Text: When using 'Target Costing,' what is the first step in the product development process?
Option 1: Designing the product and then calculating how much it will cost to manufacture it.
Option 2: Determining the desired selling price and profit margin, then designing to that cost.
Option 3: Hiring an expensive design firm to create a product that looks as modern as possible.
Option 4: Asking the factory manager what the maximum number of units they can produce is.

Question Text: What is 'Functional Obsolescence' and how can it be used as a portfolio strategy?
Option 1: When a product is designed to fail after a certain period so the user buys a new one.
Option 2: When a product is no longer useful because a newer, better technology has replaced it.
Option 3: When a product's marketing team forgets to tell the customers how to use the features.
Option 4: When a product is so complicated that only the person who designed it can use it.

Question Text: In the BCG Matrix, what is the typical path of a successful new product over time?
Option 1: Starts as a Dog, becomes a Cash Cow, then a Star, and finally a Question Mark.
Option 2: Starts as a Question Mark, becomes a Star, then a Cash Cow, and finally a Dog.
Option 3: Starts as a Star, becomes a Dog, then a Question Mark, and finally a Cash Cow.
Option 4: Starts as a Cash Cow, becomes a Star, then a Question Mark, and finally a Dog.

Question Text: What is the 'Value Proposition' of a product and why is it essential for a launch?
Option 1: The total cost of all the raw materials that went into making the finished product.
Option 2: The full positioning of a brand—the full mix of benefits on which it is positioned.
Option 3: The amount of money the company expects to make from the product in its first year.
Option 4: The physical weight of the product compared to the weight of the competition's product.

Question Text: What is 'Everyday Low Pricing' (EDLP) and which major retailer is famous for using it?
Option 1: Charging a constant low price with few or no temporary price discounts; Walmart.
Option 2: Charging very high prices every day but giving huge discounts on the weekends; Gucci.
Option 3: Changing the price every hour based on how many people are in the store; Amazon.
Option 4: Letting the customer name their own price for every item in the store; eBay.

Question Text: In 'Collaborative Filtering,' how are product recommendations usually generated for users?
Option 1: By analyzing the user's past behavior and comparing it with the behavior of similar users.
Option 2: By having a team of experts manually select products they think the user will like.
Option 3: By randomly picking products from the catalog and showing them to the user every day.
Option 4: By showing the user the most expensive products first to see if they will buy them.

Question Text: What is 'Product Adaptation' in the context of entering an international market?
Option 1: Selling the exact same product in a new country without making any changes at all.
Option 2: Modifying a product to meet local conditions or wants in a new geographic market.
Option 3: Changing the name of the company to match the local language of the new country.
Option 4: Hiring local celebrities to pretend they have been using the product for many years.

Question Text: When a company performs a 'Portfolio Audit,' what are they primarily trying to identify?
Option 1: Which employees are the most productive and which ones should be fired immediately.
Option 2: Which products are performing well and which ones should be modified or discontinued.
Option 3: How many pieces of furniture are currently in the corporate headquarters building.
Option 4: The total number of people who have ever visited the company's official website.

Question Text: What is 'Bait and Switch' and why is it considered an unethical pricing tactic?
Option 1: Attracting customers with a low-priced item and then pressuring them to buy a higher-priced one.
Option 2: Giving a customer a free worm if they agree to buy a more expensive fishing rod.
Option 3: Switching the price tags on two different products when the customer is not looking.
Option 4: Telling a customer that a product is out of stock when it is actually in the back room.

Question Text: How does 'Agile Development' differ from the 'Waterfall' method in product management?
Option 1: Agile uses long, sequential phases, while Waterfall uses short, iterative cycles.
Option 2: Agile uses short, iterative cycles, while Waterfall uses long, sequential phases.
Option 3: Agile is only used for software, while Waterfall is only used for physical products.
Option 4: Agile requires more people, while Waterfall can be done by a single person alone.

Question Text: What is 'A/B Testing' and how is it used during the launch of a digital product?
Option 1: Testing two versions of a product or marketing asset to see which one performs better.
Option 2: Testing the product with people whose names start with 'A' and then with 'B'.
Option 3: Making sure the product works in both North America (A) and South America (B).
Option 4: Testing the product on the first day (A) and then again on the second day (B).

Question Text: In 'Prestige Pricing,' why does a company set a high price for its product?
Option 1: Because the product costs much more to manufacture than any other product in the world.
Option 2: To signal high quality and exclusivity to status-conscious consumers in the market.
Option 3: To pay for the expensive lawsuits that the company is currently involved in.
Option 4: To discourage poor people from buying the product and ruining the brand's image.

Question Text: What is 'Service Blueprinting' and how does it relate to product/service management?
Option 1: A map that portrays the service system so that the different people involved can understand it.
Option 2: A set of blueprints for the building where the service will be physically provided.
Option 3: A list of all the different services that the company's competitors are currently offering.
Option 4: A photo of the uniform that the service providers will be wearing during their shifts.

Question Text: What is the 'Product Life Cycle' of a 'Fad' compared to a typical consumer product?
Option 1: A fad has a very long introduction stage and then a very slow decline over many years.
Option 2: A fad has a very quick rise to peak popularity and then an equally rapid decline.
Option 3: A fad has no decline stage because it stays popular forever once it is launched.
Option 4: A fad never reaches the growth stage and stays in the introduction stage forever.

Question Text: What is 'Bundling' and how does it help a company manage its product portfolio?
Option 1: Combining several products and offering the set at a reduced price to increase sales.
Option 2: Wrapping products in large amounts of plastic to prevent them from being stolen.
Option 3: Grouping products by the color of their packaging on the retail store shelves.
Option 4: Selling products only to customers who agree to buy everything the company makes.

Question Text: What is 'Price Skimming' and when is it most likely to be a successful strategy?
Option 1: Starting with a high price and lowering it over time; best for innovative new products.
Option 2: Starting with a low price and raising it over time; best for commodity products.
Option 3: Setting a price that is exactly the same as the competitor's price for all products.
Option 4: Letting the customer decide the price after they have used the product for a month.

Question Text: In 'Design Thinking,' what is the purpose of the 'Empathize' stage of development?
Option 1: To feel sorry for the customers because they have to pay money for your product.
Option 2: To understand the experiences and motivations of the people you are designing for.
Option 3: To tell the customers what they should want instead of listening to what they say.
Option 4: To ensure that all the designers on the team are friends and get along with each other.

Question Text: What is 'Market Segmentation' and why is it a precursor to product positioning?
Option 1: Dividing a market into distinct groups of buyers who have different needs or behaviors.
Option 2: Dividing the company into different departments based on the products they make.
Option 3: Counting the total number of people who live in a specific country or geographic area.
Option 4: Making sure that every customer receives the exact same marketing message and price.

Question Text: What is 'Heuristic Pricing' and how do consumers use it in everyday life?
Option 1: Using simple rules of thumb, like 'higher price equals higher quality,' to make decisions.
Option 2: Using complex mathematical formulas to calculate the exact value of every product.
Option 3: Asking a professional scientist to evaluate the price of every item before buying it.
Option 4: Only buying products that have a price that is a prime number, like $7 or $11.

Question Text: What is 'Reverse Engineering' and why do companies do it to their competitors?
Option 1: Buying a competitor's product and taking it apart to see how it was made and works.
Option 2: Sending a spy to the competitor's office to steal the blueprints for their new product.
Option 3: Telling the public that the competitor's product is dangerous and should be banned.
Option 4: Hiring the competitor's lead engineer and paying them to reveal all the company secrets.

Question Text: In 'Product Portfolio Analysis,' what is a 'Dog' and what is the typical recommendation?
Option 1: A product with low market share in a slow-growth market; usually should be divested.
Option 2: A product that is very popular with pet owners and should be expanded immediately.
Option 3: A product that is currently being tested and has not yet been released to the public.
Option 4: A product that is the personal favorite of the CEO and should never be discontinued.

Question Text: What is 'Anchor Pricing' and how does it influence a consumer's perception of value?
Option 1: Setting a high initial price that makes all subsequent prices seem like a good deal.
Option 2: Tying the price of a product to the weight of a physical anchor made of solid iron.
Option 3: Making sure the price of a product never changes regardless of inflation or demand.
Option 4: Setting a price that is so low that it 'anchors' the product at the bottom of the market.

Question Text: What is 'Mass Customization' and how does it affect the production and marketing mix?
Option 1: Providing individual customers with products that are tailored to their specific needs.
Option 2: Producing millions of identical products and selling them to as many people as possible.
Option 3: Letting the customer build the product themselves using parts they find in the trash.
Option 4: Hiring a famous artist to paint a unique design on one single unit of the product.

Question Text: What is 'Product Obsolescence' and what is the difference between planned and perceived?
Option 1: Planned is built-in failure; perceived is making consumers feel the old one is out of style.
Option 2: Planned is when a customer breaks it; perceived is when the company goes out of business.
Option 3: Planned is for electronic products; perceived is only for clothing and fashion items.
Option 4: There is no difference; both terms mean the same thing in the context of marketing.

Question Text: What is 'Value-Added' in the context of a product's features and benefits?
Option 1: The extra features or services that a company adds to its product to justify a higher price.
Option 2: The total amount of tax that the government adds to the final price of the product.
Option 3: The amount of weight that is added to the product during the manufacturing process.
Option 4: The number of people who are added to the marketing team to help launch the product.

Question Text: What is 'Price Anchoring' and how is it used in a restaurant menu design?
Option 1: Placing a very expensive item at the top of the menu to make other items look cheaper.
Option 2: Anchoring the menu to the table so that the customers cannot take it home with them.
Option 3: Using a heavy font for the prices so they are the first thing the customer notices.
Option 4: Listing the prices in a random order so the customer has to search for the cheapest one.

Question Text: What is 'Co-Creation' and how does it involve the customer in the development process?
Option 1: Inviting customers to participate in the design or development of a new product.
Option 2: Asking customers to pay for the development of a product before it is even designed.
Option 3: Forcing customers to assemble the product themselves after they have bought it.
Option 4: Letting customers choose the name of the company's next Chief Executive Officer.

Question Text: What is 'Product Line Pruning' and when should a product manager consider it?
Option 1: Removing unprofitable or redundant products from a line to improve overall performance.
Option 2: Adding more products to a line to make it look bigger and more impressive to buyers.
Option 3: Cutting the physical size of the products in the line to save on shipping and storage.
Option 4: Reducing the number of people on the marketing team who are working on the product line.

Question Text: What is 'Odd-Even Pricing' and what is the psychological reasoning behind it?
Option 1: Setting prices that end in odd numbers (e.g., $9.99) to make them seem significantly lower.
Option 2: Charging odd prices to men and even prices to women to see who is more price-sensitive.
